quotes.text: “personal electronic device” shall mean any portable electronic device that: (i) is capable of providing voice communication, text messaging or other data communication between 2 or more parties or devices
personal electronic device shall not include school issued or sanctioned devices that are used for a legitimate educational purpose

The department shall provide guidance, recommendations and a model policy to assist schools and districts with developing and implementing effective policies regarding the prohibition of the use of personal electronic devices on school grounds during the school day
options for secure storage of personal electronic devices during the school day, including best practices on removing physical access to personal electronic devices
Prior to finalizing recommendations, guidance and model policy, the department shall solicit public input and hold at least 1 public hearing.

Each public school or district shall adopt a policy regarding the prohibition of student use of a personal electronic device, as defined in section 40of chapter 69, on school grounds during the school day and during school-sponsored activities during the school day.

a prohibition on the use and actual possession, strictly on their person, of a personal electronic device by a student during the school day, which shall include, but not be limited to, recess, a lunch period and time in between classes.

at least 1 method for parents and guardians of students to contact students during the school day, including policies for emergency situations when it is urgent, or for a student to contact their parent or caregiver during the school day
the discipline for noncompliance outlined in the provisions shall not include the expulsion or suspension of a student
used in accordance with an individualized education program or an education plan implemented pursuant to section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973
a healthcare provider provides in writing that the possession or use of a personal electronic device is necessary to treat a health condition of a student
for time spent off school grounds travelling to or from other learning opportunities, including, but not limited to, early college, dual enrolment or vocational learning sites

Annually, not later than September 1, each public school shall notify students and the parents or guardians of students attending the school of the policy and make the policy publicly available on its website.
prior to approval, such local governing body shall solicit public input

if no policy is approved by the school committee, board or other appropriate governing body by September 1, the department’s model policy shall go into effect until such time as a local policy is approved

Nothing in this section shall limit a district from setting restrictions or standards for use of personal electronic devices on school grounds or during school-sanctioned activities beyond the school day.
Each public school or district shall annually file its personal electronic device use policy not later than September 1 with the department of elementary and secondary education

Each public school or district shall adopt a policy regarding the use of personal electronic devices as required by section 102 of chapter 71 of the General Laws before the start of the 2026-2027 school year.

Not later than December 31, 2027, the department of elementary and secondary education shall report to the senate and house committees on ways and means and the joint committee on education on the implementation of the personal electronic device use policies in schools

The department of elementary and secondary education shall provide recommendations, guidance and a model policy on the use of personal electronic devices to facilitate implementation of this act within 180 days of the effective date of this act.

proposes.text: Every public school or district would have to adopt a policy banning student use of personal electronic devices during the school day.
The state education department would write guidance and a model policy to help schools put such a ban in place.

changes.heading: What students could not have during the day

lines.text: The policy would have to bar students from using or even carrying a personal device during the school day, including recess, lunch, and time between classes.
lines.mark: recess, a lunch period and time in between classes

lines.text: A personal electronic device would mean a portable device that can make calls, send texts, or share other data.
Devices the school hands out or approves for a real educational purpose would not count as personal devices.
A district could still set rules for device use on school grounds outside the school day.
A student could use a device if it is part of an individualized education program or a section 504 plan.
A student could use a device if a healthcare provider writes that it is needed to treat a health condition.
Devices could be used while traveling off school grounds to places like early college, dual enrollment, or vocational sites.
Each policy would have to include at least one way for parents and guardians to reach a student during the day, including in urgent situations.
Punishment for breaking the rule could not include suspending or expelling a student.

changes.heading: How policies would be made and shared

lines.text: Before finalizing its guidance and model policy, the department would have to take public comment and hold at least one public hearing.
A local school committee or governing body would have to ask for public input before approving the policy.
If no local policy were approved by September 1, the department's model policy would apply until one is.
Schools would have to tell students and families about the policy by September 1 each year and post it online.
The model policy would have to cover ways to store devices securely and keep students from reaching them during the day.
Each school or district would have to file its device policy with the state by September 1 each year.

affects.text: Public schools and districts would each have to write, approve, and post a device policy.
Students would be barred from carrying or using their own phones and similar devices during the school day.
Parents and guardians would be given at least one way to reach their child during the school day under each policy.

lines.text: Your child's school would have to ban student phones and similar devices during the school day, including recess and lunch.
The school's policy would have to give you a way to contact your child during the day, including in urgent situations.
Your local school committee would have to ask for public input before approving a device policy, so you could comment even without a child in school.

notStated.text: The bill text does not mention private schools, homeschooling, or college campuses.

line.text: If it became law, each school or district would have had to adopt its device policy before the 2026-2027 school year started.
If it became law, the state department would have 180 days to issue its guidance and model policy.
If it became law, the department would have to report to legislative committees on how the policies are working by this date.

versionNotes.text: The House passed a different version of this bill, replacing everything after the enacting clause.
versionNotes.action: Committee recommended ought to pass with an amendment, striking out all after the enacting clause and inserting the text of H5349, and referred to the committee on House Steering, Policy and Scheduling

versionNotes.text: The Senate did not agree with the House changes.
versionNotes.action: Senate NON-concurred in the House amendment

versionNotes.text: A conference committee of senators and representatives was named to work out one text.

judgments.reason: The passage states each public school or district shall adopt a policy prohibiting student use of personal electronic devices during the school day.
The passage says the department shall provide guidance, recommendations and a model policy to assist schools and districts.
The passage bars use and possession on the student's person during the school day, expressly including recess, lunch and time between classes.
The definition quoted covers portable devices capable of voice, text or other data communication.
The passage excludes school-issued or sanctioned devices used for a legitimate educational purpose.
The passage preserves district authority to set restrictions on school grounds beyond the school day.
The passage names use in accordance with an IEP or a section 504 plan as an allowed circumstance.
The passage allows possession or use when a healthcare provider states in writing it is necessary to treat a health condition.
The passage covers time off school grounds traveling to or from early college, dual enrollment or vocational learning sites.
The passage requires at least one method for parents and guardians to contact students, including policies for urgent emergency situations.
The passage states discipline for noncompliance shall not include expulsion or suspension.
The passage requires the department to solicit public input and hold at least one public hearing before finalizing.
The passage requires the local governing body to solicit public input prior to approval.
The passage states the department's model policy takes effect if no local policy is approved by September 1, until a local policy is approved.
The passage requires annual notice to students and parents/guardians by September 1 and website posting.
The content on secure storage and removing physical access matches, but the passage does not state that this is a required element of the model policy.
The passage requires annual filing of the policy with the department by September 1.
The passage states schools or districts must adopt a policy but says nothing here about approving and posting it.
The passage prohibits student use and on-person possession of personal electronic devices during the school day.
The passage requires at least one method for parents and guardians to contact students during the school day.
The passage bars use and possession of personal electronic devices during the school day including recess and lunch.
The passage requires a contact method for parents and guardians, including emergency/urgent situations.
The passage requires the local governing body to solicit public input before approval, and the closing inference about public commenting adds no new specific fact.
Private schools, homeschooling and college campuses each correspond to searched terms that do not appear.
The passage requires adoption before the start of the 2026-2027 school year.
The passage gives the department 180 days from the effective date to provide guidance and a model policy.
The passage requires a report to the ways and means committees and the joint committee on education by December 31, 2027 on implementation.
The entry records a committee recommendation and referral to House Steering, not House passage of a different version.
The entry records the Senate non-concurring in the House amendment.
The entry records only a Senate appointment of conference committee members, not that representatives were also named.
